- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot in early days following sentiment surges.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or volatile; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends; adjust for recent sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to premature retracement forecasts.
- In high-sentiment periods (especially >1.5), model often overpredicts 3–5 days ahead; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% for sentiment >1.0.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overfit recent highs; apply downward bias to avoid overconfidence in short-term peaks.
- For sentiment < -0.5, model underreacts to price drops; increase forecast downward adjustment by 2–3% per day of negative sentiment.
